title: Quality-first ~90 GiB memory-matched expert-pruning x quantisation sweep for MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL
status: design; no model compute has run; every measurement slot is null until measured

unit_conventions.byte_rule: Every budget comparison is decided on exact integer bytes. Decimal GB is 10^9 bytes; GiB is 2^30 bytes; the two are never mixed. No approximate parameter math anywhere: every figure derives from memory-report.json / inventory.json fields or exact integer formulas stated below.

digest_basis: inventory.json source.files[].lfs_sha256 (71 LFS-digested files) + recorded sizes for all 90 files, recomputed against the on-disk tree
manifests/models/mimo-v2.6-flash-rl/memory-report.json derived from the same safetensors-header inventory
digests verified = recorded sha256 values match the bytes on disk at the pinned revision
source_weights.rule: Every candidate is constructed ONLY from these original weights. The tacodevs MLX checkpoint (and its published tensor-sensitivity work) is PRIOR INFORMATION and is never a construction source.

budget.basis: Text-model resident weight payload = retained expert instances + non-expert text classes with the router row-sliced to the retained count. Auxiliary components (mtp/vision/audio/dflash: components.* except text) are recorded separately and never netted into this budget; KV cache and runtime headroom are excluded.

rounding_rule.method: round_half_up(x) = floor(x + 0.5); REAPxx is defined as the PERCENT OF EXPERTS PRUNED PER LAYER

byte_constants.affine_byte_rule: bytes = logical_parameters * bits // 8 + (logical_parameters // group_size) * 2  (int8 scale + int8 zero point per group; every referenced tensor's parameter count is divisible by its group_size, so all products are exact integers)

router_bytes_per_retained_index.formula: 47 * (4096 * 2 bytes per BF16 gate row + 4 bytes per F32 bias entry)

non_router_non_expert_native_bytes.formula: 8894573440 - 98614272; equals the exact inventory class-row sum (attention + dense_ffn + embeddings + norms)

mxfp4_bpw_exact.note: U8 nibble-packed weights + per-32 scale bytes; not interchangeable with ROCm FP4 GGUF formats

byte_constants.pure_native_text_formula: resident(R) = R * 628359168 + R * 385212 + 8795959168; validated against all five memory-report.json prune_candidates[].native_text_payload_bytes rows (256/192/176/160/144)

native_dense_row_sliced.note: router: exact dense row scaling of BF16 gate weight + F32 bias to the retained count (known:true per docs/pruning-integrity.md); no packing cost invented

protected_class_table.adaptation_rule: Class-table precisions are PROTECTION CEILINGS: a class never drops below its ceiling, and stays bit-exact native while the budget allows. Second-generation quantization is applied class-by-class ONLY where the matched budget requires it, and every application is recorded in that candidate's second_gen_applied list.

non_expert_class_bytes_native.source: exact sums over inventory.json tensors (component=text, non-expert)

construction_rules: Construct every candidate ONLY from the pinned original Xiaomi weights (source_weights); never from any MLX or community checkpoint.
No MLX requantization EVER: the tacodevs checkpoint is never read as a tensor source, and already-quantized MLX/GPTQ tensors are never converted into production formats.
Surviving native MXFP4 (QAT) tensors keep their represented values: bit-exact packed-weight + scale copy (allocation rows bit_exact=true); no re-encoding.

BF16/FP16 intermediates are COMPUTE-ONLY: decoding MXFP4 -> BF16 does NOT restore pre-QAT/full-precision weights. Re-encoding from such an intermediate is second-generation quantization and is allowed only where allocation_table marks second_gen=true.

Second-generation quantization is applied class-by-class ONLY where the matched budget requires it, and every application (class, exact scope, bytes before/after, reason) is recorded in recipe.second_gen_applied - an empty list means none.
Affine byte math is exact integer: logical_parameters * bits // 8 + (logical_parameters // group_size) * 2; every affected parameter count is divisible by its group_size (documented per row).

Router handling follows docs/pruning-integrity.md: gate weight + e_score correction bias sliced row-wise to the retained count with exact dense row scaling (post_remap_stored_bytes_known=true); routing stays top-8 over the retained set; no packing cost is ever invented.
Expert selection comes from an external REAP quality map (--selection schema of src/mimo_halo/pruning); shape-only seed maps are structural placeholders and are never quality maps.
Byte budgets follow the accounting rule of docs/pruning-integrity.md: kept + unchanged + exact post-remap router; auxiliary components (mtp/vision/audio/dflash) recorded separately, never netted in.
Every candidate records exactly where second-gen was applied; candidates are otherwise bit-exact reconstructions of the pinned source.

staged_evaluation.principle: Design now, run later. Stages run in order; bad candidates die at the CHEAPEST stage that can kill them; stage 4 runs only for Pareto-frontier candidates.
staged_evaluation.kill_criteria_status: PLACEHOLDER - every threshold below is null on purpose and MUST be calibrated against the observed stage-1 spread (all five candidates + the original-MiMo control) before any stage executes. No fixed threshold numbers are invented in this design.

kill_criteria.calibrates: max delta-perplexity, max KL, min agreement floors - to be set from the stage-1 spread across candidates + original control
min per-slice agreement, max long-context degradation, max pathological-generation counts - set only after stage 1 results exist

stages.name: reduced benchmark suite
measures: reduced benchmark scores within practical limits

kill_criteria.calibrates: min score deltas vs original on the reduced suite - set only after stage 2 results exist

stages.name: expensive full benchmarks (Pareto frontier only)
stages.applies_to: candidates on the quality-vs-resident-bytes Pareto frontier after stage 3
stages.kill_criteria_status: selection stage - no kill; feeds the decision rule

decision_rule.ranking: Rank survivors by QUALITY at matched size (~90 GiB, +/-2%). Quality evidence = the staged-eval record (perplexity/KL/agreement, trajectories, pathological scan, benchmarks).
decision_rule.throughput_exclusion_reason: All throughput numbers are PRE-OPTIMISATION diagnostics: the current runtime may have better kernels for one datatype than another, an implementation artifact, not a compression property. A high-quality candidate is never rejected for poor current throughput; a worse candidate is never selected for a lucky kernel.
decision_rule.pareto: Report the quality-vs-resident-bytes Pareto frontier among stage-3/4 survivors; infeasible or killed candidates stay listed with their exact numbers and kill stage.
decision_rule.promotion: Top 2-3 candidates by quality proceed to runtime optimisation afterwards; the concurrency-scaling sweep runs only on those promoted candidates.
decision_rule.matched_size_enforcement: A candidate outside the +/-2% band may not be built as specified; its recipe must be re-planned (class-by-class, recorded) until its planned total is inside the window.

pp.method: llama-bench batched prompt processing (scripts/benchmark_matrix.py bench mode); batch-size dependent, NEVER labeled concurrency

c1_decode.method: decode at 1 concurrent stream against one server (scripts/benchmark_matrix.py serve mode vocabulary)

c4_decode.method: 4 actually-concurrent HTTP decode streams; aggregate_tokens_per_s over the concurrent wave

c8_decode.method: 8 actually-concurrent HTTP decode streams; aggregate_tokens_per_s over the concurrent wave

theoretical_bytes_per_token.method: exact active-weight streaming formula (docs/experiments/compression-sweep.md, Performance diagnostics section); integer bytes

active_weight_bandwidth.method: theoretical_bytes_per_token / measured decode seconds per token

concurrency_scaling_sweep.gating_decision: Concurrency/runtime tests are SHELVED until a quality baseline exists (original-MiMo control plus surviving candidates measured through stage 1-3). Runtime optimisation - and this sweep with it - stays gated behind the quality frontier: no concurrency number may be produced, compared, or acted on before then.
concurrency_scaling_sweep.applies_to: serious candidates only: those surviving to the Pareto frontier / top 2-3 quality selection
concurrency_scaling_sweep.label: PRE-RUNTIME-OPTIMISATION

per_point_records.aggregate_decode_tok_s: aggregate decode tokens/s across all streams at this concurrency
per_point_records.per_stream_tok_s: aggregate / concurrency, plus per-stream distribution if the harness exposes it
per_point_records.pp_throughput_tok_s: prompt-processing throughput measured alongside (batch-size dependent; never called concurrency)
per_point_records.ttft_ms: time to first token per stream (unit: milliseconds)
per_point_records.ram_bytes: resident RAM while serving this point (unit: bytes)
per_point_records.kernel_dispatch_cliffs: obvious kernel/dispatch cliffs observed at this point (notes; empty if none)
per_point_records.expert_overlap: if practical: unique experts touched and overlap across streams as concurrency rises (record availability honestly when not practical)

goals.hardware_throughput_sweet_spot: the concurrency where aggregate TPS stops improving materially
goals.interactive_sweet_spot: the concurrency where aggregate TPS stays high without per-stream speed becoming unpleasant

rules: Do NOT assume powers-of-two or higher concurrency is better; measure every listed level.
If throughput drops at one concurrency level, profile it as a possible kernel/dispatch artifact BEFORE treating it as a hardware limit.
All numbers are PRE-RUNTIME-OPTIMISATION and must be labeled as such: use them to understand scaling behaviour and spot suspicious cliffs, NEVER to pick the compression-quality winner.
Quality-first rules are unchanged: concurrency results never reorder the quality ranking; only promoted candidates are measured.

harness.scripts/benchmark_matrix.py: serve mode vocabulary: concurrency = actually parallel HTTP requests against one llama-server (thread pool, one socket per request); aggregate_tokens_per_s derived from server-reported predicted token counts over the wave wall time; statuses ok/timeout/failed/parse_error; model recorded by basename only (no local paths in reports). Extend concurrency.levels to [1,2,4,6,8,12,16]. bench mode: PP points are batch-size knobs and are NEVER reported as concurrency.
harness.scripts/burst_replay.py: schedule vocabulary: schema_version 1, events[{t_s, kind, prompt_tokens, gen_tokens}], scale; per-event latency_s/start_lag_s/predicted_tokens give TTFT and inter-token latency for the interactive sweet spot; 'successful requests per replay wall-hour' is schedule-specific observed throughput.

prior_information.statement: Prior information used, nothing copied: every byte figure in this config derives from OUR inventory of the ORIGINAL Xiaomi weights; the tacodevs work contributes only ordering priors and vocabulary.
used: tacodevs published precision allocation as sensitivity prior: 141 projections = 93x affine b3 g128, 22x native mxfp4 b4 g32, 18x affine b2 g128, 8x affine b3 g64; other text tensors 8-bit affine g64; attn_bits 8; embed_bits 16; lm_bits 8 (sources: manifests/baselines/tacodevs-reap25/normalized.json precision_summary + published_evaluation.distribution.compression_eval; docs/baselines/tacodevs-reap25.md)
Quant-spec vocabulary bits/group_size/mode incl mxfp4 from tests/test_tacodevs_reap25.py _spec_cycle()

Their published calibration/held-out/on-policy metrics (PPL 9.271 -> 9.529, KL 0.8315, top1 79.5%; on-policy ALL 90.4% / code 90.8% / agent 88.5% / reasoning 94.2%) as context only - never reused as our measurements, never claimed reproduced
docs/experiments/memory-matched.md feasibility arithmetic (superseded by reference, unchanged on disk)
not_copied: No tacodevs/MLX tensor values, packed switch_mlp checkpoints, GPTQ artifacts, or their per-layer/per-projection precision map enter any candidate or any byte figure.
Their sensitivity ordering is not our measured sensitivity and not task-success evidence; we reproduce the class table as a PRIOR with its source pointer and adapt it to our budget.
The published REAP25 checkpoint proves nothing about optimal REAP25, and avoiding requantization proves nothing about REAP40/45 viability: the sweep exists to find the actual quality cliff.
Our class precisions differ from theirs where our budget demands (embeddings Q6 vs their embed 16; router/norms raised above their 8-bit) - deviations are recorded per class above.
our_sources: manifests/models/mimo-v2.6-flash-rl/inventory.json (tensors[] exact stored_bytes/logical_parameters per class; source.files[] digests)

claims_and_prohibitions: Design status only: no inference functionality, no benchmark, and no calibration number is claimed by this config; every measurement slot starts null/empty.
Fit claims use exact integer bytes only; prose-unit matching is prohibited.
Missing measurements stay null/unavailable; they are never zero and never inferred.
Distribution metrics (ppl/KL/agreement/NLL) are controls, not capabilities; they are never cited as task success.
Never requantize the tacodevs MLX checkpoint; never treat BF16/FP16 intermediates as restored pre-QAT weights.
Throughput (including the concurrency sweep) never selects the compression-quality winner.
